Ecommerce Performance Dashboard

An e-commerce business operating across multiple European regions is growing in revenue but facing quiet pressure on margins, rising return rates, and inconsistent delivery performance. This dashboard goes beyond top-line revenue to answer where profit is actually coming from — and where it is being silently lost.

About the Dataset

Star schema with one central fact table — FactOrderLine — containing 46 columns covering every order line: units sold, revenue, cost, discount, return status, fulfillment details, and marketing allocation. Connected to 9 dimension tables: DimDate, DimProduct, DimCustomer, DimGeography, DimPromotion, DimFulfillment, DimSalesChannel, DimReturnReason, and DimCohortAge.

Data Cleaning & Transformation

All cleaning done in Power Query. DAX kept clean.

  • Standardised headers and data types: Date columns originally in proper date format, intentionally converted to integer keys (e.g. 20250329) to serve as join keys connecting FactOrderLine to the dimension tables.
  • Handled expected nulls in ReturnDateKey: Nulls represent orders never returned — left as null and handled at DAX measure level to avoid misrepresenting return volumes.
  • Text cleaning across all dimension tables: All text columns trimmed and cleaned to strip hidden characters and whitespace that would break table relationships.
  • Deduplication on dimension tables: Duplicate rows removed to guarantee one row per entity — ensuring clean one-to-many relationships with FactOrderLine.
  • Columns renamed for clarity: Key fields renamed from technical database conventions to clear business labels.
  • All DAX measures calculated explicitly: CM%, Return Loss, On-Time Delivery Rate, Allocated Marketing Cost %, and Product Cost Rate % built as explicit DAX measures — keeping the model efficient.

Data Model

Star schema — FactOrderLine at the centre.

FactOrderLine connects to 8 dimension tables via foreign keys. A separate Calculated Measures table and KPI Selector are kept off the fact table to maintain a clean, efficient model.

Selected Visuals

Four visuals. Four business stories.

So what — Marketing & Commercial team

CM% vs Discount Rate by Campaign

Clearance 3 sits at -11.6% CM — every sale costs the business money. Bundle & Save at 28% proves value-led campaigns protect profit. Stop Clearance 3 and redirect budget to what works.

So what — Product & Finance team

CM% vs Product Cost Rate by Category

Beauty runs 46.3% CM while Electronics — the top revenue category — sits at 2.8%. The business is chasing volume in its least profitable category. A portfolio shift to Beauty and Fashion would significantly improve overall margin.

So what — CRM & Retention team

Net Sales per Customer by Segment & Lifecycle

VIP customers deliver €700+ at 25%+ margin. Deal Seekers spend actively but at only 10% margin. Protect VIP retention and reduce discount depth for Deal Seekers who take margin without loyalty.

So what — Operations & Product team

Return Loss by Return Reason

"Changed mind" leads at €25K in losses — not a quality problem, a pre-purchase expectation problem. Better product descriptions and sizing guides will fix this without touching supply chain.

Business Questions & Decisions

Five questions. Five decisions supported.

  • 1. Is the business generating profitable revenue or just volume?

    At 19.4% CM, most revenue is consumed by product costs, discounts, and fulfillment. Growth without margin improvement is unsustainable.

    → Decision: Pricing and cost structure review

  • 2. Which campaigns are helping and which are destroying margin?

    Clearance 3 at -11.6% and Weekend Flash at 1.4% are losing money or barely breaking even and should be stopped immediately.

    → Decision: Campaign budget reallocation

  • 3. Which product categories are actually profitable — not just popular?

    Electronics drives highest revenue but holds the lowest CM at 2.8%. Beauty at 46.3% is nearly 17x more profitable per euro of revenue.

    → Decision: Portfolio and investment strategy

  • 4. Which customer segments are worth investing in for growth?

    VIP customers deliver the highest margin and spend. Deal Seekers spend at 10% margin. Converting Growth customers into VIP tier should be the CRM priority.

    → Decision: CRM and retention investment

  • 5. Why are customers returning products and what is it costing?

    €102.90K in return losses. "Changed mind" at €25K tells us the fix is better pre-purchase content — not product quality improvements.

    → Decision: UX and product content improvement

Insights & Recommendations

What the data says. What the business should do.

  • Kill Clearance 3. At -11.6% CM it is a cash drain. Reallocate to Bundle & Save which runs at 28% margin.
  • Shift investment from Electronics to Beauty and Fashion. A 10% shift in marketing spend to Beauty could significantly improve overall CM without reducing order volume.
  • Build a VIP retention programme. VIP customers deliver €700+ at 25%+ margin. Losing one VIP costs more than acquiring three new customers.
  • Fix the pre-purchase experience. €25K lost to "Changed mind" returns. Better product images, sizing guides, and descriptions will reduce this without touching supply chain.
  • Review Paid Social ROI. At 11.8% CM vs Organic Search at 24% — rebalancing toward SEO and content would significantly improve marketing efficiency.
